interest: Captures U.S. customs seizing Japanese naval codes and Allied tracking of Japan's prewar merchant shipping recall.
overview: This file comprises State Department correspondence, consular telegrams, and intelligence reports from June and July 1941 documenting global surveillance and diplomatic tensions surrounding Japanese merchant shipping. It details the diplomatic controversy over U.S. customs seizing Japanese naval codes from the whaling ship Nisshin Maru, Allied countermeasures like British stevedoring slowdowns in Chile and Philippine petroleum restrictions, and widespread intelligence confirming Japan was recalling its commercial fleet to home waters ahead of military expansion.
